text: Auto-restart on checkout change (2026-09): Stavros asked that restarts happen only when the git checkout changes, so detection uses git HEAD of the package checkout. A hash of the loaded .py files was proposed and rejected by him: it would also fire on uncommitted hand edits and on non-checkout installs. He runs the daemon under systemd; os.execv (same PID) was chosen over exit-and-let-systemd-restart because the README unit uses Restart=on-failure and tmux users have no supervisor. Deliberately not built: a config flag (feature is naturally limited to checkout runs), a drain mode that stops new work while a change is pending (a busy daemon may never idle; add only if seen in practice), and a running QA serve blocking restart (a long QA would block all updates).
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text:
Known, accepted limits of the web UI backend (STA-757), all rooted in the decision not to change orchestrator.py for this feature:

1. Stop pressed in the first moments after Start (before the orchestrator has created its state entry) does not stop the turn: the orchestrator treats a triggered ticket with no state entry as a new ticket and its pipeline moves it back to In Progress. A second Stop, once the agent process exists, works through the existing mid-turn-stop path. Fixing the first case needs an orchestrator change.

2. LocalTracker.transition_to is deliberately asymmetric. The orchestrator may not move a ticket from Done/Draft to In Progress or QA (a worker that already read its input would otherwise undo the user's Done), but it MAY move Done to Needs Input, because the dirty-workspace refusal in tick step 3 does exactly that and records the state it left the ticket in. The first version of the guard blocked all targets; the review caught that this made the next tick delete the dirty workspace after a single Done click. If the guard is ever widened again, uncommitted work gets deleted. A real-Orchestrator test (two ticks after one Done) pins this.

3. Reopen picks its target state by reading the StateManager: still tracked -> Needs Input, not tracked -> In Progress. Both simpler rules were tried and are wrong: always Needs Input lets a reply be typed before the new-ticket pipeline picks the ticket up, and on the path without a session snapshot that reply never reaches the agent; always In Progress strands a still-tracked ticket (accidental Done then quick Reopen) showing 'working' with nothing running.

4. Uploads: 50 MB per file is enforced by the web layer, but attachments.process_attachments still has its own 50 MB total cap per turn, so two large files in one message make the daemon skip one and post its 'skipped attachments' notice. Left alone because attachments.py is shared with Linear and GitHub.

5. The Anthropic title call was never exercised against the real API during development (no key available); only the request shape, API version header (2026-10-21) and model id were checked against the vendor docs. If titles never appear, look at the WARNING log line from webui/title.py first.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: One-command first run (SYM-41): 'uvx symphony-linear' with no config creates ~/symphony with a generated config. Rejected: (1) opening a browser automatically on first run; Stavros chose to print the URL and password instead (also useless over SSH on a headless host). (2) Free-port search; a fixed port keeps the generated config stable. (3) An auth-free localhost mode; see uwxghy, the sandbox shares the host network. (4) Creating the workspace in the current directory; uvx is often run from ~ or inside a repo, and clones would litter it. (5) Running without bwrap installed; Stavros deferred it as a bigger job, for now startup fails with install hints.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text:
Mid-turn comments are discarded rather than queued for the next turn, and the reason is the human's, not a technical one.

The obvious fix for a comment posted while a turn is running is to queue it and feed it to the next turn (make the end-of-turn last_seen_comment_id write land on the last comment the turn consumed instead of on the bot's own final comment; list_comments_since is positional, so everything after it replays). That was designed and costed at about 15 lines. It was rejected.

Stavros's reasoning: a mid-turn comment is written without having seen the agent's reply. Once the reply lands, the comment is often stale — he would have written something different. Replaying it makes the agent act on an instruction the human had already superseded. He would rather read the reply and copy-paste a fresh comment than have a possibly out-of-date one acted on automatically.

So the daemon posts 'I did not read this — I'm mid-turn' and drops the comment. Note README's Limitations section previously claimed mid-turn comments were queued and delivered next turn; that was never true, and the text was corrected rather than the behaviour.

A second alternative was rejected on scope, not merit: having each pipeline advance last_seen_comment_id at the moment it consumes its input. That removes the need for the in-memory _turn_input_marker map entirely (about four lines), but a daemon restart mid-turn would then stop replaying the triggering comment — _rerun_interrupted_turn would take its 'session id but nothing pending' branch and park the ticket with 'reply to continue'. That is arguably consistent with the same anti-stale-replay argument above, and may be worth revisiting, but it changes a documented recovery invariant and leaves part of the interrupted_turns machinery unused.

We explicitly rejected the WORKFLOW.md-style configurable prompt template approach that the openai/symphony SPEC.md describes. The system prompt and ticket prompt format are hardcoded in the orchestrator. Reasoning: this tool is built for solo personal use with stable workflow needs; adding a YAML-front-matter + Liquid-template loader and a file watcher would have multiplied the complexity for no concrete benefit at MVP scope. If users start wanting per-repo prompt customization, the cleanest reintroduction is to look for a `.symphony/prompt.md` in the repo at bootstrap time and use it instead of the hardcoded one. Don't bring back hot-reload or front-matter unless there's a real second use case driving it.

SYM-14 (Nov 2026): the Needs Input ntfy push is skipped while Stavros is watching that ticket's page. Idle limit is 10 minutes: Stavros first wanted 1-2 minutes (after that he has gone away), then chose 10 because when he is near the computer the tab title count is enough of a signal. Only that ticket's page counts, not home or other tickets. The signal rides on the existing poll GET (?active=1). A separate POST heartbeat was rejected as an extra endpoint and request. A reviewer also suggested requiring a poll-only header so a Markdown image cannot set presence. That was rejected: the worst case is one push suppressed for about 15 seconds.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The 2026-08 layout change (<root>/<id>/{repo,attachments,tmp}) shipped as a clean break with NO migration, per Stavros: he deletes all tickets before upgrading, so in-flight state doesn't matter. A migration was considered and rejected — partly because it would be mostly futile anyway: OpenCode namespaces sessions by project/worktree path, so moving the clone from <root>/<id> to <root>/<id>/repo breaks 'opencode run --session <id>' resume regardless; a migration could only clear session ids (fresh session, lost agent context), not preserve them. Keep this in mind for any future change that moves the repo path.

SYM-4 (Nov 2026): web UI notifications use ntfy (optional webui.ntfy block; one JSON publish when the daemon moves a ticket to Needs Input). Web Push was proposed by the ticket and rejected in favour of ntfy: it needs a service worker, VAPID keys, a subscription store, pywebpush/cryptography, HTTPS, and on iOS a home-screen install, for the same result on Stavros's phone (his main device). Also decided: web UI backend only (Linear/GitHub notify on their own; covering them would mean hooking the orchestrator), and the message carries identifier + title only, never reply text (the reply is posted after the transition, and ticket content should not go to a third-party ntfy server). Supersedes the 'notifications deferred' note in ksyxye.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text:
Rejected: a user-specifiable agent launch command in config.

When adding the pi harness (Aug 2026) we designed, then dropped, an `agent.command` config key holding argv templates with {prompt}/{session}/{model}/{files} placeholders, so any pi-compatible harness could be added without code.

Dropped because the band it covers is nearly empty. pi and omp differ by ONE flag (--auto-approve vs --no-approve) plus the binary name; everything else (-p, --mode json, --session <id>, --model, @file attachments, trailing prompt positional) is already identical. A fork that keeps the JSON protocol will almost certainly keep those flags too, and a fork that CHANGES the protocol needs parser work that no launch command can supply. The real coupling is the JSON event schema, not the argv.

Costs that decided it: a placeholder mini-language, validation that can only check placeholder presence and never semantics, and a bad failure mode — omit --auto-approve on an omp-like fork and turns do not error, they hang until the idle watchdog kills them at turn_idle_timeout_seconds. That reads as a flaky agent, not a config mistake. Adding a harness in code is smaller than a user writing a correct template.

Revisit only if a third-party fork appears that we cannot just ship support for. The convergence the maintainer wants is already delivered by the shared parser (pi_protocol.py) plus agent_runner: with those shared, a new pi-family harness costs roughly ten lines of argv.

SYM-18 (Nov 2026): the web UI is an installable PWA with a manifest only and no service worker. Stavros wanted only 'add to home screen, opens standalone'. Chrome has not needed a service worker to install since 108, and offline mode has no use for a live view of the daemon. His auth is Tinyauth forward-auth in front of Basic auth, so the manifest link needs crossorigin=use-credentials. Installing behind Tinyauth has not been tested. Web Push on top of this is still to be discussed (see fdyakc).
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: SYM-33 (Nov 2026): Stavros asked for the README to sell Symphony as an easy, sandboxed web UI with modern features that works with your coding agent. Linear and GitHub get only a short mention there, and all reference detail lives in docs/ (seven files, one per topic). Do not grow the README back into a reference: new detail goes into docs/. README images and links are absolute GitHub URLs because the README is also the PyPI page, where relative paths were already broken; the cost Stavros accepted is that they point at master and show broken in a branch preview until merge. He also accepted that the package and command stay named symphony-linear although the pitch leads with the web UI (a rename was treated as out of scope, not rejected). On the sandbox pitch his position is that the gh login and the SSH agent can be closed by hiding their paths (sandbox.hide_paths), so the docs describe the default as open on purpose plus how to close it, instead of saying the sandbox cannot prevent a push. Screenshots use fake tickets from misc/screenshots.py, kept in the repo by his choice so they can be regenerated after UI changes; desktop is light theme and phone is dark theme to show both with four images. Empirical: Chrome cannot start its own sandbox inside the Symphony bwrap sandbox, so the script passes --no-sandbox.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: SYM-39 (Nov 2026): Stavros wants agent questions to be a first-class thing the UI can design against. Agreed design: the agent writes a callout ('> [!QUESTION] text' with a bullet list for choose-one, a '- [ ]' task list for choose-many, no list for free text) and the web UI renders it as an answerable card. This deliberately bends the dumb-pipe decision (xjgnpt): the agent now gets one output-format sentence, but still no tool and no knowledge of the tracker. Decisions that came from Stavros: (1) the format note must be 'really short, to avoid wasting turn space'; he accepted one sentence of about 45 tokens sent on EVERY message (not only the first prompt), web UI backend only. (2) Answers live on the card, not in the reply composer. The first proposal made the composer text the only state (a tap wrote a quoted block into the textarea and the card parsed it back); he rejected it as odd ('half the answers in the composer and half on the card'), so answers are stored separately and joined with the composer text only at Send. (3) Amending is a pencil on each option that turns the label into an editable field, plus an 'Other' row; one text field per card was replaced by this. Select-and-edit in one tap was his first idea and was dropped: it opens the phone keyboard on every tap and conflicts with tap-to-deselect in choose-many. (4) He wants multiple select in the first version. Deferred, not rejected: answer buttons on the lock-screen push notification, the reading aids (question strip at the top of a reply, first-sentence previews and question badges on collapsed sections), and dictation inside card fields. Rejected as annotation methods: a JSON fenced block, a reserved 'Questions' heading, an agent-side question tool (three harnesses, parity), and per-section type markers. Agreed order: ship the note alone first and watch real replies, because agent compliance against each agent's own system prompt was untested when this was planned.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text:
Daemon-posted comments are tagged with a visible Markdown footer of the form `*Symphony · {kind}*`, appended at the tracker-adapter layer (linear_tracker.py / github_tracker.py) from a `kind` string supplied by the caller (e.g. "workspace", "final", "error", "context: 37,074 tokens"). Detection uses the helper `is_bot_comment(body)` in tracker.py, which checks for the substring `*Symphony · ` (middle dot is U+00B7). This replaced the old HTML-comment sentinel (`<!-- symphony:bot -->`) because Linear's renderer does not strip HTML comments, making the previous sentinel visible and ugly in the UI.

Two alternatives were considered and rejected this round:

1. Invisible zero-width characters as a sentinel (ZWSP / ZWNJ, etc.). Rejected as hacky, fragile, and prone to leaking via copy/paste into human comments.

2. Filtering by token-owner user id via `viewer { id }`. Rejected because when running with a personal API token, this would silently drop comments typed by the same human whose token is used, causing the daemon to ignore genuine human input.

The marker approach also removes the need for a separate bot user identity (the previous current_user_id / bot_user_id / bot_user_email machinery was all dropped), letting users run the daemon with their own personal API token.

Symphony refuses to delete a dirty workspace on the first cleanup and bounces the ticket back to Needs Input. The user accepted two costs explicitly when this was designed: (1) in no-push setups every ticket is dirty by definition (local-only commits are the only copy of the work), so closing any ticket takes two moves to Done - this is intended, it reads as a confirmation prompt; (2) orphan directories accumulate forever with no garbage collection, including full clones plus whatever .symphony/setup built. Ticket deletion is deliberately exempt from the guard: the user's reasoning is that deleting a ticket almost never happens by accident, while moving a ticket's state happens constantly. Rejected alternatives: auto-commit or auto-push before deleting (credentials are hidden in the sandbox by design), a config switch for a looser 'uncommitted files only' test, a force label, an expiry on the refusal, and simply keeping every dirty directory without ever bouncing the ticket (the user wanted the tracker-visible stop signal). If disk growth becomes a problem, GC is the thing to add - not a weaker dirtiness test.

STA-757 (Nov 2026) added a web UI. Stavros's stated intent: the web UI should SUPERSEDE Linear eventually ('the Linear interface is a bit cumbersome'), and it is fine that tickets created in the web UI are not visible in Linear or GitHub. That is why it was built as a third tracker backend with its own on-disk tickets (webui: config block, one backend per daemon still), not as a viewer/replier over Linear tickets, which was the first proposal and was dropped as throwaway work.

Not built, on purpose: showing Linear/GitHub tickets in the same UI, migrating in-flight tickets, and a daemon with several trackers at once (the orchestrator assumes one tracker everywhere; judged a high-risk refactor for a temporary transition need). During a transition the expected setup is two daemons with two workspace dirs.

Stavros explicitly deferred, not rejected: a live view of the agent's steps inside a running turn ('nice to have, Linear doesn't have it either, for later'). Also deferred by scope: notifications (the unread mark and the '(N) Symphony' tab title are the stand-in), named projects, search.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: UX review (Nov 2026), decisions from Stavros: (1) Live turn view still deferred (ksyxye); the cheaper middle step was chosen instead: 'last output N ago' on the ticket page, counting stdout AND stderr like the idle watchdog (stdout-only rejected: OpenCode stdout is silent while a subagent works, so healthy turns would look stalled). Not on home rows. (2) Retry button posts the fixed comment 'Retry.' instead of a new orchestrator action; shown only for a failed Needs Input ticket; placed in the composer actions, not on error alerts (an alert is history). No shortcut. (3) The model can change between turns from the composer select; it applies on Send/Retry, saving on change was rejected. /api/v1 cannot change it. (4) Needs Input rows show a Haiku one-line summary of the latest agent reply (same key and fixed model as titles; no fallback without a key; not on other rows, ntfy or the API). Rejected by Stavros: QA visibility (serve URL link, serve running indicator), 'I don't use it enough'. Rejected: collapsing the ticket page Details block on the phone, because the page opens scrolled to the first unread entry or the bottom, so the header is already out of view.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: STA-475 (2026-10): Stavros stated the rule: the agent only works while the ticket is In Progress, so moving a ticket to ANY other state mid-turn must stop the turn (QA and untriggered states have their own stop paths; Needs Input and other active states use the new step-4 stop). He accepted that comments feeding the stopped turn are dropped (same as udbvzt) and accepted the risk that a failed In Progress transition at turn start gets the turn stopped on the next tick. An in-memory 'this turn moved the ticket to In Progress' flag to close that gap was considered and rejected as not worth the extra state.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: SYM-45 (Nov 2026) question cards on the ticket page: Stavros asked for tabs instead of the cards shown one after another, with digits 1-0 picking options. Decisions: only cards that are direct DOM neighbours (nothing between them) form one tabbed panel; moving every card of a reply into one panel was rejected because prose or headings the agent writes between questions would be separated from its question. A single card gets no tab strip but the digits still work. A choose-one pick advances to the next tab; the last tab stays put (Stavros: 'stay put for now'; moving focus to Send was rejected because a stray Enter would send). With several groups, keys act on the last-used group, else the first visible group with an unanswered question. Stavros accepted that while questions are live a digit no longer starts a reply (type-to-reply); on a free-text tab digits still start a reply.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: SYM-3 (Nov 2026) web UI keyboard shortcuts: j/k + Enter = move through ticket rows, navigation is 'g' then a second key (gn = New ticket, gt = Tickets, ga = Archive, gr = Repositories), and status changes are a two-key sequence 's' then a second key. SYM-22: New ticket was originally the single key 'c', but on the ticket page type-to-reply needs 'c' to type (replies start with 'can you...'), so 'c' did nothing there; Stavros chose to replace 'c' with 'g n' on every page rather than keep 'c' (unshifted-only) and lose lowercase-'c' replies. Do not reintroduce 'c'. Single-key status actions (d = Done, s = Stop, etc.) were proposed and replaced because an accidental Stop drops the comments that fed the turn and an accidental Done can clean up the workspace. Second keys map to a FIXED target state, not to the visible buttons in order, so a key always means the same thing. Current mapping (SYM-3 follow-up, Nov 2026): sn = to Needs Input (Stop, Back to Needs Input, or Reopen on a Done ticket, whose real target is still chosen by the server), sq = Send to QA, sd = Done. History: originally s1/s2/s3 (Stavros's first ask); he found digits hard to remember. 'so' for open was rejected because many replies start with 'So' and type-to-reply would turn that into Stop; for the same reason only an unshifted lowercase s/g arms a prefix ('SQL' must type). SYM-9: Stavros accepted one key (now sn) for Reopen, so do not add a separate key. A status menu popup was rejected twice (SYM-3, and again in the follow-up in favour of letters); instead, while a prefix is armed, small key badges show on the controls it can activate (state buttons for s, dock links and the New ticket button for g). SYM-9 added the '?' help dialog (static list, same on every page, no visible button because the phone has no '?' key). Not built: j/k on the ticket page.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: A bwrap integration test whose fixture lives under /tmp silently tests nothing about path visibility. run_in_sandbox binds the per-ticket tmp dir over /tmp, so anything the test placed under /tmp is already invisible inside the sandbox for reasons unrelated to what is being tested. This produced a passing, vacuous test for the workspace-root masking fix: it still passed when the masking helper was neutered to return only the configured hide paths. Put sandbox visibility fixtures outside /tmp, and always confirm the test fails with the protection disabled before trusting it.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: SYM-15 (Nov 2026): Stavros supplied a new 'orbits' icon (three arcs: violet #8B6CFF, cyan #19C3E6, orange #FF9838 on an indigo tile) and chose to re-tint the whole web UI palette to it rather than change the icon only. Mapping: neutrals indigo-tinted instead of green-tinted, the 'your turn' accent is the icon's orange (was saffron #f2b632), links and focus are violet (darker #4d38c7 on light because the icon's own violet is only 3.3:1 there). Deliberate: the icon's cyan has no role (the design keeps one loud colour); the danger tokens were left unchanged although orange sits nearer to the danger red than saffron did, to be revisited only if Stavros sees the dark-theme Delete button and Needs Input tag as too alike. misc/design_reference.html was NOT updated and no longer matches the shipped colours or icon (tnufng says the stylesheet was copied from it; that is now true for layout only). Rejected: an SVG favicon/logo beside the PNG (ntfy accepts only PNG/JPEG, so two files would have to stay identical; icon.png stays the single file per pcnmct). misc/icon.svg is the source with the attachment's C2PA provenance block removed at Stavros's request. The README shows the same static PNG at the top at his request. The ntfy Android client caches icons up to 24 hours, so an icon change takes up to a day to show on the phone after it reaches master.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: SYM-5 (Nov 2026): ntfy notifications carry a Symphony icon (Android only; Stavros's phone is Android), also used as the web UI favicon and title-bar logo. Final design: the icon is webui/static/icon.png, served behind Basic auth at /static/icon.png (ICON_PATH) for the browser; ntfy always gets NTFY_ICON_URL, the same file on raw.githubusercontent.com master, because the ntfy client cannot send credentials. Tried and reverted the same day: an unauthenticated /public/icon.png route with a Route.public flag. Stavros runs a forward-auth proxy, which blocks it anyway, and removing it keeps Basic auth on every request with no exception. Rejected: GitHub Pages (same file, more setup); a config option for the icon URL. Accepted cost: the ntfy icon only changes once pushed to master, and forks show the upstream icon. public_url moved from webui.ntfy to webui at Stavros's request because it is not ntfy-specific; it stays under webui, not the config root, because only the web UI backend has a URL; it now only drives the click link. Moved with no alias because it was in no release.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: SYM-43 (Nov 2026): /api/v1 exposes question cards read-only, as a 'questions' list on each agent-reply comment, from the same parser as the page. Decisions from Stavros: answering stays a normal POST comment (the guide recommends the browser's layout); a structured 'answers' field that the server turns into the body was rejected because it would duplicate the assembly in static/questions.js in Python. Questions are listed on every agent reply, not only the newest unanswered one (stateless). Card prose is deliberately not in the JSON; it stays in body. Browser reply_answers are not readable or writable via the API.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: SYM-3 (Nov 2026): the Needs Input dot on the 'Tickets' nav link counts every Needs Input ticket including the one currently open (Stavros confirmed). On the phone layout the ticket and editor pages hide the bottom dock, so the dot is also drawn on their 'Back to tickets' link; the phone is the main device. The home page on phone hides its own Tickets link, and that is accepted because the list itself shows the Needs Input group.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text:
Maintainer intent: converge on fewer harnesses, not more.

Stated while adding pi (Aug 2026): the direction is "one harness for everything", not "more different harnesses". A separate backend per coding-agent fork is explicitly the thing to avoid, and a proposal that adds one should be pushed back on.

What this means in practice: the shared seams (pi_protocol.py for the NDJSON schema, agent_runner.py for sandbox/watchdog plumbing) are where new agent support belongs. Per-agent modules should shrink to argv construction. opencode.py is the standing exception — its event schema genuinely differs (top-level sessionID, tool_use trimming), so it cannot join the pi family without a real protocol shim.

Feature parity across harnesses is a requirement, not a nice-to-have: anything one harness supports (model override via Model: labels, attachments, context-token reporting, session resume) the others are expected to support too.

2026-08 (STA-127): a turn failed because the Anthropic API returned repeated 'AI_APICallError: Overloaded' for claude-opus-5; OpenCode retried ~6 times over 95s on its own, then exited 1. When this was raised, the user explicitly chose NOT to add a Symphony-side retry or backoff for transient provider errors, and instead to move failed tickets to the tracker's Needs Input state so a human reply drives the retry. The 'no auto-retry on failure' invariant therefore holds deliberately even for failures that are known to be transient — do not 'improve' it into an automatic retry without asking.

STA-115: the 'OpenCode freezes forever' reports were all one upstream bug — 'opencode run' answers permission.asked only for the top-level session (session-id filter before the auto-approve branch), so an ask from a task-tool subagent is never answered and the turn hangs. Three separate hangs were confirmed in the wild, all on external_directory asks from @developer/@code-reviewer subagents. Two facts that made this look infinite rather than slow: the production config (which lives outside the repo, in the workspace dir) sets turn_timeout_seconds to 18000, and a hung turn also holds one of the 5 pool workers for that whole time. Diagnosis technique worth reusing: ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log is shared by all instances but every line carries run=<8 hex> and session ids, so you can locate exactly where a hung turn stopped; a hung run's only remaining activity is an hourly 'cleanup prune=7.days' line, whereas an actively working run (subagents included) never went quieter than 38s. Stavros will file the upstream bug; the fix on our side is deliberately server-side (OPENCODE_PERMISSION), not CLI-flag-side, because every --auto-style flag sits behind the same broken filter.

SYM-2 (Nov 2026): the editor's repository dropdown reads a named list in <workspace>/tickets/repos.json owned by LocalTicketStore. Stavros rejected a config.yaml key ('I should be able to add a repo from the web UI very easily'). Rules he set: each repo has a name so the dropdown does not show long URLs; removing a repo only removes it from the dropdown and never touches existing tickets (tickets keep storing the full URL, not a reference). Design choices: the list is seeded once from existing tickets at store load (never in a GET); an inline-added repo joins the list only on Start, because the editor's autosave would otherwise add half-typed URLs. Rename and reorder were left out (remove and re-add instead).
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Refines zqgxcm (STA-276, 2026-09). A ticket that enters QA with no state entry AND no session snapshot (never worked by an agent) now gets its workspace cloned and .symphony/setup run in the background, then serve starts; no agent turn runs until a human comments. The user confirmed that serving the ticket's remote branch, or a fresh branch off the default branch when none exists, is the intended behaviour for 'start in QA directly'. Setup runs as a background task (not inline in the tick) because setup scripts can take minutes and the tick holds a lock. Tickets with a session snapshot still get the zqgxcm refusal. Restart during QA setup is deliberately unhandled, same gap as the new-ticket pipeline.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: SYM-19 (Nov 2026): ntfy removed completely at Stavros's request, once Web Push was confirmed working in Chrome. Web Push is now the only notification channel for the web UI backend. Decisions: Web Push stays always on with no config (the only off switch is the browser's site settings); an old webui.ntfy block is a hard config error with no shim, because ntfy was never in a release. Supersedes the ntfy design in fdyakc and pcnmct (the public GitHub icon URL survives as PUBLIC_ICON_URL in webui/push.py, for the service worker) and the 'ntfy stays optional' line in tkpccd.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: WebhookServer injects on_wake by creating a per-server _HandlerWithWake subclass with on_wake as a class attribute. Calling it via self._on_wake() binds 'self' as the first arg (because Python treats functions stored on a class as methods); to invoke the raw callable, use type(self)._on_wake() in BaseHTTPRequestHandler subclasses. This pattern is also used for _webhook_secret (set as a server instance attribute, accessed via self.server._webhook_secret in the handler). If the injection pattern is refactored, audit both call sites — the current shape is slightly unusual but minimal.

SYM-44 (Nov 2026): /api/v1 got CORS with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * because Stavros calls it from a browser page on another origin, through his forward-auth proxy. That proxy must let unauthenticated OPTIONS under /api/v1 through, since a preflight never carries Authorization; this is proxy config, outside the repo. Stavros chose to make the anonymous guide (GET /api/v1) CORS-readable too, and accepted that any page can then detect a running daemon. Rejected: an origin allow-list or config option (YAGNI; the bearer-only namespace has no ambient credential to borrow).
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: SYM-17 (Nov 2026): /api/v1 is a JSON API for Stavros's personal AI agent, which runs OUTSIDE the sandbox and should 'create and monitor tickets'. Agents inside the sandbox were explicitly excluded; giving them the token would let a prompt-injected agent start more agents and read every ticket. Goal stated by Stavros: 'agent-friendly, self-explaining, point an agent to it and it understands immediately', hence a hand-written Markdown guide at GET /api/v1, {error, hint} errors and allowed_actions on each ticket. Rejected: OpenAPI (harder for an LLM to read, more to maintain, no codegen need); allowing Basic auth when Origin is absent (weakens the browser CSRF defence); webhooks/long polling (the agent polls with updated_since and a comment cursor). Auth is a separate bearer token (webui.api_token) only on /api/v1; Stavros confirmed his forward-auth proxy lets bearer requests through. Repo rename (name only, never URL) exists in the API at his request, although the UI still has none (qmhsun). Not built: file uploads via the API, pagination.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Observed 2026-09 (STA-334): the Linear API returns intermittent HTTP 503s and 30s read timeouts (~10 of ~714 turns in 30 days lost a state transition; comment fetches and issue polls fail at similar rates but self-heal next tick). Pipeline transitions now retry transient errors (orchestrator._transition_with_retry). Rejected alternatives: caching workflow state ids per team (halves exposure only, stale-id risk); per-tick reconciliation of tracker state vs internal status (would fight humans who move tickets to QA/Done deliberately); retrying inside LinearClient for all calls (would block the single-threaded poll loop during outages, and the loop already re-runs those calls).
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Observed in production (2026-07, STA-81 incident): any orchestrator failure path that posts a tracker comment WITHOUT changing the ticket's state self-amplifies — the posted comment fires a Linear webhook, which wakes the poll loop immediately, which retries the same failure and posts again, yielding a sub-second retry+comment-spam loop instead of one attempt per poll interval. The established pattern (used by _bail_qa_no_workspace and now the serve-start-failure path) is: transition the ticket state FIRST, and post the comment only if the transition succeeded — the state transition is the de-dup that breaks the loop. Any new failure path that comments on a ticket must follow this pattern.

Observed Nov 2026 in production: agents working on Go repos put the module cache (GOMODCACHE/GOPATH) under the per-ticket /tmp or inside repo/, because ~/go is read-only in the sandbox. Go makes that cache 0555, so plain shutil.rmtree in workspace.remove() failed with PermissionError; the orchestrator had already dropped the state entry, so 15 ticket dirs (~22 GB, 1-2 GB each) were orphaned with only an ERROR log. Fix: remove() retries once after an fd-based, O_NOFOLLOW walk adds u+rwx to dirs. Rejected: GOFLAGS=-modcacherw in the sandbox env (Go-only, agents override it); keeping the state entry on failure so the next tick retries, and an orphan-dir sweep (YAGNI once read-only trees delete). A shared cache via sandbox.dir_map would also save the per-ticket downloads; not configured as of this fix.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: SYM-18 (Nov 2026): Web Push added beside ntfy at Stavros's request, only so notifications carry the installed app's identity and icon. This supersedes the Web Push rejection in fdyakc. ntfy stays optional and unchanged. Decisions: always on for the web UI backend with no config; the bell only turns push on (turning it off is in the browser's site settings); http-ece plus our own VAPID signing over httpx, not pywebpush (rejected because it brings aiohttp, requests and py-vapid). Considered and not done after review: a list of allowed push-service hosts (brittle, and only an authenticated user can register an endpoint); hiding httpx debug logs of endpoint URLs (an endpoint is useless without the VAPID private key). Not yet tested in a real browser or behind Tinyauth.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text:
Web UI behaviour choices that came from Stavros's own workflow (STA-757), so they should not be 'tidied up' later:

- The reply composer is never disabled while the agent works; only Send is. He writes notes there during a turn for his next reply, and the text is saved on the server so it follows him between phone and desktop. This sits beside the older decision that mid-turn comments are discarded, not queued (bxrkzk): the UI now prevents the mid-turn send instead of posting 'I did not read this'.
- The composer has a large mode that must keep the last lines of the agent reply visible: he reads the reply and writes at the same time.
- Agent replies collapse by TOP-LEVEL heading only, closed by default. Nested collapsing was offered and rejected: 'too much clicking, I just want an easy way to keep things tidy'.
- Drafts exist because he parks thoughts for later.
- Phone is the main device, desktop is also heavy use.
- No model picker with raw model names: only the aliases defined under models: in config.yaml are offered (the design mock's 'Default (name)' entry was rejected). SYM-2 (Nov 2026) changed the control from radio chips to a <select> with a plain 'Default' first option, at Stavros's request: radio chips could not be cleared back to the agent default.
- Uploads accept any file type up to 50 MB (he uploads zips and html files, not just screenshots). Images still go to the model as image input; other files only land in the attachments dir.

Titles: he does not want to write titles. Generating the title by running the configured coding agent once in the sandbox was proposed and rejected as too heavyweight; instead the daemon calls the Anthropic API directly with an optional webui.anthropic_api_key and a deliberately hardcoded model id (claude-haiku-5-5, 'no need to customize this'). Without the key the editor requires a title field. Do not add a model/prompt setting for this without a reason.

The visual design is in misc/design_reference.html (a design-tool bundle; the shipped stylesheet was copied from it).
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: SYM-9 (Nov 2026): the editor's repository picker is Ctrl+K (Cmd+K), chosen by Stavros, who has around 30 saved repositories, so fuzzy matching was worth it over native select type-ahead. Ctrl+K works inside text fields on purpose: the user usually reaches for the repository right after typing the ticket text, so a plain 'r' (ignored while typing, like the other shortcuts) was rejected. The picker is a modal dialog that only sets the native #repo select and fires change; replacing the select with a custom combobox was rejected because it would need its own no-JS path and would lose the phone's native picker.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text:
We removed the `opencode.model` config option (was at `AppConfig.opencode.model`). The reasoning: OpenCode's own configuration already selects a model, and in the workflows people actually run — multi-step agentic loops, tool use, code edits — overriding the model from Symphony's outer layer doesn't add value. The option was effectively dead config surface.

Don't reintroduce a model selector at the Symphony level without a concrete use case. If model choice ever needs to vary per-ticket (e.g. cheap model for triage, strong model for implementation), the right place is OpenCode's config or a per-project setting, not a single global string in Symphony's config.

The removal was a breaking change (`feat!:`); existing configs with an `opencode:` section fail loudly at load via pydantic's `extra="forbid"`.

STA-289 (2026-09): When QA stops a running turn (or the daemon repairs a stale working ticket found in QA after a restart), last_seen_comment_id is anchored to the QA notice, so the triggering comment and mid-turn comments are deliberately not re-read by the next turn. The user accepted this trade-off. Carrying skipped comments into the next turn via a second 'include but do not trigger' marker was considered and rejected as more complexity than one extra human reply is worth.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: SYM-39 follow-up (Nov 2026): after the first real use Stavros missed the agent's recommendation: the note said only 'recommended first', so agents stopped writing '(recommended)' and the card had nothing to show. Decision: the note now also asks for the literal marker '(recommended)', the card shows it as a tag and strips it from the answer text, and marked options start SELECTED. Preselection was Stavros's explicit choice among three offered options; the architect had advised against it because a Send made for another reason (for example a counter-question typed in the composer) then also sends the preselected answers and can approve the agent's pick by accident. Treating the first option as recommended without a marker was rejected (false pick when the agent has none; meaningless for choose-many). Stavros also wants the questions exposed in the /api/v1 agent API later; not designed yet.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: SYM-42 (Nov 2026): Symphony runs without bwrap, unsandboxed, but only as a quick trial. This replaces item (5) of bqnajp, where running without bwrap was deferred. Stavros's goal was only that a trial is quick and easy without installing bubblewrap; macOS support and hosts where bwrap cannot run were not the goal. He chose an automatic fallback when bwrap is missing and rejected an explicit switch (a sandbox.enabled config key or a --no-sandbox flag): bubblewrap is never explicitly disabled, and with bwrap installed the sandbox is always used. When told that a trial has a config from its second start on, and that real installs can also lack bwrap (a systemd unit with a narrow PATH, a workspace copied to a new host, a removed package), he asked that anything other than a trial keeps failing with an error, and picked both conditions: built-in web UI tracker AND started from a terminal. Rejected for that rule: web UI tracker alone (a web UI service would fall back silently) and a marker key written by the first run (anyone can write it by hand, so it becomes an explicit switch). The warning is one startup log line by his choice; a web UI banner and a note in each ticket's workspace comment were offered and declined. sandbox.dir_map with no bwrap is a startup error and not a warning, in his words because someone with a dir_map is way past a quick trial and something has gone wrong if bwrap is unavailable. He accepted on recommendation: the same clean environment as the sandbox (not the daemon's environment), a process-group kill only in unsandboxed mode, and no equivalent of --die-with-parent.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text:
Web UI auth (STA-757): HTTP Basic auth only, credentials in the webui: block of config.yaml. The ticket originally asked for 'Tinyauth support'; Stavros dropped that during design ('never mind Tinyauth, we just auth with basic auth'). Tinyauth still works in front without any code, because Tinyauth can inject Basic credentials after login (tinyauth.apps.<app>.response.basicauth.*) — that was Stavros's own idea and is why Basic auth was picked.

Rejected:
1. Trusting the Remote-User header from a forward-auth proxy. The sandbox shares the host network, so a sandboxed coding agent can call the UI port on localhost and forge the header; the UI can create tickets, i.e. start more agents, and read other tickets. Any header-trust scheme needs a secret the sandbox cannot read; the Basic password in config.yaml (masked from the sandbox) is exactly that. Do not add an auth mode that has no such secret.
2. OAuth/OIDC client in the daemon (Tinyauth v5 can be an OIDC server). Stavros: 'seems like a bit of a hassle'. About 200 lines of security-sensitive code for a single-user tool.

Related consequence that is easy to miss: browsers attach Basic credentials to cross-site requests automatically, so the same-origin check on non-GET requests is the CSRF defence, not an extra.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Setup-error retry loop fires off historical comments when last_seen_comment_id is None. _save_setup_error (and the ProjectConfigError branch of _resume_pipeline) used to persist last_seen_comment_id=None when the error comment couldn't be posted to the tracker. On the next poll tick, _has_new_human_comment(tid, None) returns all comments, so any historical human comment satisfied the 'new comment' gate and re-fired _new_ticket_pipeline every poll interval — symptoms: workspace metadata comment posted multiple times, 'New ticket pipeline starting' repeating every poll. Fix establishes a three-tier baseline hierarchy at both error-save sites: (1) error_comment.id if posted, (2) existing last_seen_comment_id if non-None, (3) most-recent comment id via Tracker.list_comments_since(tid, None) with a graceful None fallback on tracker failure. Whenever you add a new error path that sets setup_error or transitions to failed, preserve this invariant: last_seen_comment_id must never be None when comments exist on the ticket.

A daemon restart is the daemon's fault, not the human's, so restart recovery must re-run the interrupted turn by itself rather than ask the human to nudge the ticket. Two alternatives were rejected when this was decided: (a) keep the bounce to Needs Input and only fix the misleading comment wording, and (b) make the bounce truthful by advancing last_seen_comment_id so the ticket genuinely waits for a reply. Both were rejected because they make the human do work after every restart. The retry cap exists only to stop a turn that keeps dying from being replayed forever; it is not a general retry policy, and 'no auto-retry on failure' still holds for turns that actually complete and fail.

Timeout comments include the salvaged partial message UNTRUNCATED by explicit user decision (STA-79): the partial output is mostly tool-call titles, which _assemble_message already summarizes to one line each, so real-world size is modest. Don't add a truncation cap without revisiting that. Same session also chose to salvage the sessionID from partial stdout on first-turn timeout so retries resume instead of restarting — resume-after-SIGKILL was assumed OpenCode-safe (same as daemon crash mid-turn) but not empirically verified; if resumes after first-turn timeouts ever misbehave, the fallback is to null session_id in the initial-pipeline timeout handler again.

OpenCode V2 migration (Oct 2026): qktuby's OPENCODE_PERMISSION workaround was removed. In V2 a subagent hitting the only remaining default 'ask' (reading .env) completed without hanging under --auto, external_directory defaults to allow, and doom_loop no longer exists. If V2 turns start hanging on permission asks again, re-check this first. Also observed but not handled: V2 lets the model launch subagents in the background (tool input background:true); untested whether 'opencode run' can exit while one is still running. If subagent work is seen cut off, that is the likely cause.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Symphony deliberately keeps the agent ignorant of Linear. The agent's final assistant message on a turn becomes a Linear comment; Linear comment replies are fed back as the agent's next user message. The agent has no Linear tool, no awareness of ticket state, no special prompt structure for asking questions. This 'dumb pipe' shape was chosen because (a) it kept the integration surface tiny and language/agent-agnostic, (b) it removed the need to design agent-side tool protocols for ask-human/post-comment, and (c) it made comment concatenation (when the user posts multiple replies between polls) trivial: just glue them with author/timestamp headers and feed as one user message. The cost is that the agent can't ever 'know' it's on Linear, which means it can't reference ticket metadata or other tickets unless we shove them into the prompt explicitly. If someone ever wants the agent to manipulate Linear state directly (e.g. close the ticket, attach a PR link), they would need to break this abstraction — adding an MCP/tool on the agent side and giving the daemon a delegation model. Don't add this casually.

STA-220: linear.trigger_label became nullable. Stavros found adding the Agent label per ticket too much friction because every ticket in his workspace is meant for agents. With null, a ticket is triggered by active state (In Progress/Needs Input/QA) plus a Repo external link on its project. Two alternatives were considered and rejected: a new linear.team config field to scope the poll (extra config; Repo link already mandatory so it scopes for free), and flipping the default to no label (rejected to avoid surprising existing installs). Accepted consequence: in null mode any human-owned In Progress ticket in a repo-linked project gets picked up. GitHub trigger_field deliberately left as is.

Ticket→session mapping (StateStore.sessions) is deliberately maintained lazily: snapshotted only at cleanup time and consulted only at _new_ticket_pipeline start, while TicketState remains the live copy of session_id/last_seen_comment_id. A full split (moving those fields out of TicketState into the sessions map) was considered and rejected — it touches ~a dozen call sites across resume/recover/failed paths plus a state.json migration, for identical observable behavior. Entries are durable (not deleted on rehydrate; only pruned when the ticket itself is deleted) so repeated done→back cycles stay correct. Also rejected: skipping cleanup for done tickets entirely — would cost one get_issue call per done ticket per tick plus unbounded disk until Linear auto-archive.

User decisions (STA-271): secrets are one KEY=value file per repo at <secrets_dir>/<host>/<owner>/<name>.env, not a directory per repo, and the user chose <name>.env over an extension-less name for editor highlighting. The daemon deliberately never parses the file or injects values into the env (user chose 'file only'); scripts source SYMPHONY_SECRETS_FILE. Rejected: per-repo entries in config.yaml (user did not want to edit config and restart to add a secret), an index file mapping names to repos, env-var injection (leaks into every subprocess/env dumps), running setup outside the sandbox, and committed encrypted secrets (key must still reach the sandbox).
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text:
STA-169 added OMP as a second coding-agent CLI alongside OpenCode. Stavros chose to keep BOTH rather than replace OpenCode, explicitly because he wanted the abstraction (agent_runner.py + one adapter per CLI); replacing outright would have been noticeably less code and was the cheaper option on offer.

Three things were considered and rejected, so there is no code to comment on:
- Per-project and per-ticket ('Agent: omp' label, mirroring the existing 'Model:' labels) selection. Selection is global only, one config field, matching how the tracker backend is chosen.
- Profile isolation via 'omp --profile symphony'. It would isolate the daemon's sessions and caches from interactive OMP use, but also isolates auth, so it needs a separate login. Stavros said share the default profile for now.
- Relaxing the 'models:' alias validator to accept OMP's fuzzy model names ('opus'). Left alone: label values that miss the alias map already pass through verbatim, so 'Model: opus' works with no config entry, and only the alias map itself is restricted to provider/model.

Accepted unverified risk, agreed as ship-and-watch rather than build-for: five concurrent pool workers share one ~/.omp containing several SQLite WAL databases (agent.db, history.db, models.db) plus run/daemons. OpenCode has the same shape and works, but OMP leans on SQLite harder. Nothing was built to defend against it.

STA-156: tracker comments now post only the agent's closing reply, not the whole turn trace. Rejected alternatives, so nobody rebuilds them: (a) keeping the trace in a collapsible <details> block -- Linear does not render raw HTML, so it would show as literal markup (GitHub would work, but one behaviour for both backends was preferred); (b) 'answer first, trace below a rule/blockquote' -- keeps every comment long, which was the complaint. The accepted cost is that narration between tool calls is lost: if the agent explains something mid-turn and closes with 'Done.', only 'Done.' is posted. The chosen mitigation is prompt-side (a sentence in _build_initial_prompt telling the agent to put the whole answer in its final message), NOT re-adding the trace. The timeout path deliberately keeps the full trace (see wdfrgs).

QA-on-missing-workspace deliberately does not auto-reclone. When _reconcile_serve picks a winner whose workspace was deleted (typical cause: the ticket was previously moved out of an active state, which triggers cleanup), we comment+transition out of QA rather than running prepare() to clone fresh.

Reason: the agent never git-pushes (sandbox hides credentials by design — see AGENTS.md). The agent's commits therefore live ONLY in the local workspace clone. If we re-cloned for QA, _git_switch_branch would fall through to 'git switch -c' against the remote default branch, and .symphony/serve would silently run against base-branch code — i.e. QA would 'start' but serve the wrong thing. Refusing to start is the safer failure.

The supported flow is to QA *before* moving the ticket to Done. Done→QA isn't recoverable in the current architecture.

This would only become a sensible feature if push-from-agent becomes the norm (so the branch is reachable from the remote). The user has separately mentioned wanting Symphony to optionally not auto-create per-ticket branches (push target/creds/PR being out of Symphony's scope) — that change, if it lands, may revisit this decision.

STA-200 added a per-project tier to the Model: label override (issue label > project label > agent default). Putting the per-project model default in .symphony/config.yaml was offered as the cheaper option and Stavros rejected it outright: that file is per-REPOSITORY, not per-Linear-project. One repo can be the target of several Linear projects, so a model default there would be a per-repo setting wearing the name 'project'. His words: 'this isn't per-repo, it's not suitable.'

Do not revisit this by adding a 'model:' key to ProjectConfig. If someone genuinely wants a per-repo model default later, it is a separate feature with a separate name, not this one. Note also that .symphony/config.yaml would need the model resolved after the clone; today _new_ticket_pipeline resolves the model before it resolves the repo URL.

Also considered and not built: reading a per-project default on the GitHub backend. This is not a design choice we can revisit — GitHub Projects v2 has no project labels at all (ProjectV2 has no labels field and does not implement Labelable), and GitHub issue labels are per-repository while a project spans repos. The only routes would be parsing ProjectV2.readme/shortDescription or a project-id-keyed map in daemon config; both were declined as out of scope.
